claim: Taipei 101 Observatory general admission (floors 88F/89F) is NT$600; the 101st-floor outdoor add-on is NT$380; Skyline460 premium experience is NT$3,000; hours are 10:00-21:00 daily.
quote: Adult NT$600 ... 101st floor add-on NT$380 per person ... Skyline460 NT$3,000 ... Weekdays/Weekends & National Holidays 10:00 - 21:00

claim: A high-speed elevator carries visitors from the 5th floor to the 89th-floor observatory in 37 seconds, and the 101st-floor ticket is only valid for one hour so should be used first.
quote: high-speed elevator from the 5th floor to the 89th floor in just 37 seconds ... The 101st floor entry ticket is only valid for an hour

claim: National Palace Museum adult admission is NT$350, open Tuesday-Sunday with the museum holding over 700,000 artifacts; nearest access is MRT Shilin (Red Line) plus a short bus ride.
quote: Adult tickets are NT$350 ... Take the MRT Tamsui-Xinyi (Red) Line to Shilin Station, exit at Exit 1, cross the road to the bus stop and board Bus R30, 255, or 304

claim: The National Palace Museum is Taipei's most important museum, rewarding 3-4 hours of patient browsing, though large calligraphy and painting galleries can be skippable for those short on time.
quote: the single most important museum in Taipei ... rewards 3-4 hours of patient browsing ... Large galleries on calligraphy and painting can be skippable

claim: Elephant Mountain (Xiangshan) is a free, steep ~180m hike reachable in a 7-10 minute walk from Xiangshan MRT (Red Line), taking about 1.5 hours round-trip, with the Six Boulders viewpoint giving the best Taipei 101 skyline view; golden hour/sunset is most popular but crowded.
quote: Most visitors begin at Xiangshan MRT Station on the Taipei Metro Red Line ... about 1.5 hours (return) ... The trail's iconic viewpoint is the Six Boulders ... Xiangshan is free, close to central Taipei

claim: Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall is open daily 09:00-18:00 with free admission, sits at its own MRT stop on the Green and Red lines (Exit 5), and runs an hourly changing-of-the-guard ceremony from 10:00 to 17:00.
quote: open daily from 9am to 6pm ... Admission to Chiang Kai Shek is free ... changing of the guard ceremony takes place every hour on the hour from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM

claim: Longshan Temple (founded 1738) in Wanhua is open daily 06:00-22:00 with free entry, a blend of Buddhism/Taoism/folk religion, and sits 30 seconds from Longshan Temple MRT (Blue Line); incense burning was banned in 2020 for air quality.
quote: Longshan Temple opens daily from 6 AM to 10 PM, with free entry ... Longshan Temple Station (Blue and Green Lines), a 30-second walk ... founded in 1738 ... In 2020, Longshan Temple banned incense burning

claim: Dihua Street in Dadaocheng is Taipei's oldest commercial street, lined with dried-goods and Chinese herbal-medicine shops, tea sellers, the Dadaocheng Visitor Center (free traditional-dress dress-up), and historic temples; needs 1-3 hours and offers renowned riverside sunsets.
quote: Dihua Street ... considered the oldest street in Taipei ... long line of traditional Chinese Herbal Medicine shops ... Dadaocheng Visitor Center has traditional clothing that you can put on ... most beautiful sunsets in Taipei

claim: Dalongdong Bao'an Temple, with construction begun in 1804, won a 2003 UNESCO Asia-Pacific Heritage Award for its restoration and is noted for colorful walls, intricate carvings, and elaborate ceilings.
quote: construction commenced in 1804 ... In 2003, the temple was inducted into the UNESCO Asia-Pacific Heritage Awards for Culture Heritage Conservation ... colorful walls and intricate carvings

claim: The Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall (Xinyi District, completed 1972) closed its main hall on 26 Feb 2024 for a major NT$1.6 billion renovation expected to last until late 2026, though the surrounding Chungshan Cultural Park stays open.
quote: closed on February 26, 2024, and ... expected to be closed to the public until late 2026 ... NT$1.6 billion (US$50.6 million) in funding ... Chungshan Cultural Park will remain open

claim: 228 Peace Memorial Park, with landscaped gardens, arched bridges and open lawns, commemorates the February 28, 1947 uprising and ensuing repression in which thousands of Taiwanese were killed.
quote: 228 Peace Memorial Park commemorates a solemn history ... on February 28, 1947, martial law was declared ... thousands of Taiwanese people were killed

claim: Da'an Forest Park is a 1994-opened ecological green space in central Taipei lined with camphor, cajuput, ficus and maple trees, accessed directly via an exit at Daan Park Station on the MRT Red Line.
quote: ecological park with a forest-like environment ... camphor, cajuput, ficus and maples ... officially opened in 1994 ... Daan Park Station on the Red Line, which has an exit that leads directly into the park

claim: Some travelers explicitly skip the National Palace Museum (found boring, 'endless halls of artifacts') and Dihua Street ('just a street'), while rating Taipei 101, Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall, Longshan Temple and night markets as the true first-timer must-sees.
quote: National Palace Museum: The author found it boring ... Dihua Street: Dismissed as just 'a street' ... Chiang Kai Shek Memorial Hall, described as 'huge, super impressive' ... Lungshan Temple, noted as 'beautiful, full of smoke, incense'

claim: Shilin is Taipei's largest and most famous night market, open ~4PM to midnight daily, reached via MRT Red Line Jiantan Station Exit 1; budget NT$300-600 for small bites including fried chicken fillet, oyster omelet and flame-grilled cube steak.
quote: Shilin is open 4 PM to midnight daily... reach it via MRT Tamsui-Xinyi (Red) Line, Jiantan Station, Exit 1... Must-eat items include Large Fried Chicken Fillet, Oyster Omelet, and Flame-grilled Cube Steak.

claim: Raohe is a compact single-path market beside Songshan Station (MRT Green Line, Exit 5), whose signature is the Michelin Bib Gourmand Fuzhou black pepper pork bun (~NT$70) baked in a clay oven; arriving 5PM beats the dinner crowd.
quote: Raohe is a single-path market... MRT Green Line... Songshan Station, then use Exit 5... the most famous food for sale is the Michelin Bib Gourmand Award-winning Black Pepper Pork Bun... Around NT$70 per bun.

claim: Raohe has held six Michelin Bib Gourmand awards since 2018 and is widely considered the best Taipei night market for serious food lovers.
quote: Raohe has held six Michelin Bib Gourmand awards since 2018. It is widely considered the best night market in Taipei for serious food lovers.

claim: Ningxia is a compact, food-focused local-favorite market (5PM-11:30PM, near Shuanglian/Zhongshan MRT) with multiple Michelin Bib Gourmand stalls: Yuan Huan Pien oyster omelet, Fang Chia shredded chicken rice, Rong's pork liver soup, and Liu Yu Zi fried taro balls.
quote: Yuan Huan Pien Oyster Egg Omelette... Fang Chia Chicken Rice... a Bib Gourmand street food entrant in its 2019 Taipei Bib Gourmand selection... Rong's Pork Liver... Liu Yu Zi... Operating Hours: 5:00 PM to 11:30 PM daily

claim: Tonghua (Linjiang Street) night market is a laid-back, rarely-crowded local market near Taipei 101 via Xinyi Anhe MRT Exit 4, serving stinky tofu, gua bao, lu rou fan, sheng jian bao and crispy fried chicken, half food and half fashion.
quote: This market seldom gets really crowded... stinky tofu, cuttlefish stew, Taiwanese hamburgers (gua bao), braised pork rice (lu rou fan)... Xinyi Anhe MRT Station... The market is half food and half fashion for the younger crowd

claim: Huaxi Street (Snake Alley) near Longshan Temple MRT Blue Line Exit 3 has lost its snake-meat trade (banned in the 2000s) but remains gritty and atmospheric with tasty eats beside Longshan Temple.
quote: The Snake Alley of old is gone... the area remains gritty and interesting, with Longshan Temple another point of interest and Huaxi market providing some tasty eats... get off at Longshan Temple Station... Exit 3

claim: Ximending is the neon youth shopping playground often compared to Tokyo's Harajuku, while Da'an is the leafy cafe-lined district for travelers wanting a local feel.
quote: Ximending is the loud, neon, K-pop-infused playground for younger travelers... compare it to Tokyo's Harajuku... Da'an is the leafy, cafe-lined neighborhood favored by travelers who want to feel like locals.

claim: Dihua Street in the historic Dadaocheng district is Taipei's oldest street, lined with dried-goods, herb, tea and souvenir shops, offering a slow authentic vibe with few tourists, sitting between the Tamsui River and Ningxia Night Market.
quote: Dihua Street runs through the historic Dadaocheng neighborhood... between the Tamsui River and Ningxia Night Market... lined with shops selling dried goods, medicinal herbs... the oldest street in Taipei... barely any other tourists

claim: Taiwan's oyster omelet (oysters in sweet-potato-starch batter with egg and greens, pan-fried) traces to Fujian's Minnan region, and stinky tofu is fermented in a brine of milk, vegetables and meat.
quote: the oyster omelet... traces its origins back to... China's Minnan region of the Fujian province... fresh, plump oysters folded into a batter of sweet potato starch, egg and greens... stinky tofu... brine of fermented milk, vegetables and meat

claim: Beef noodle soup, considered Taiwan's national dish, was created in Taiwan by Kuomintang veterans from Sichuan who fled mainland China and served it in military dependents' villages.
quote: created in Taiwan by Kuomintang veterans from Sichuan province who fled from mainland China... served the dish in military dependents' villages... the national dish of Taiwan

claim: Bubble tea originated in 1980s Taiwan, with Chun Shui Tang in Taichung and Hanlin Tea Room in Tainan both claiming to have invented it around 1986; a 2019 court ruled it unpatentable, assigning credit to neither.
quote: Two tea houses — Chun Shui Tang in the central city of Taichung and Hanlin Tea Room in the southern city of Tainan — both claim to have invented the drink in 1986... a Taiwanese court ruled in 2019 that bubble tea was not patentable

claim: Jiufen is reached via train to Ruifang (30 min express / 50 min local, NT$73) then bus 827 or 788 (20 min, ~NT$15); total trip is about 1 to 1.5 hours.
quote: Take the northbound train from Taipei Main Station to Ruifang Station. The journey takes 30 minutes for express trains, or 50 minutes for local trains. The cost is NT$73... bus number 827 or 788... around 20 minutes and costs around NT$15 each way.

claim: Direct bus 1062 runs from Zhongxiao Fuxing MRT Station to Jiufen Old Street every 20-30 minutes, and crowds and travel time worsen on weekends and holidays.
quote: Bus 1062 is the easiest way to get to Jiufen - it starts from Zhongxiao Fuxing Station in Taipei and you alight at Jiufen Old Street bus stop. The bus typically comes every 20-30 minutes.

claim: Xinbeitou hot spring village is under 20 minutes from central Taipei by MRT (red line to Beitou, then transfer to the short Xinbeitou branch line), with green/white/iron sulfur spring types.
quote: You can reach Beitou in less than 20 minutes from Taipei by hopping on the MRT... transfer at Beitou Station and take another subway on Xinbeitou Line to Xinbeitou MRT Station.

claim: Thermal Valley (Geothermal Valley) is a free, steaming turquoise sulphur pool near the MRT, and private onsen rooms should be booked in advance while public baths like SweetMe are gender-separated.
quote: Thermal Valley... a bubbling and steaming turquoise pool... one of only two green sulfur hot springs in the world... free entrance... Private onsen rooms... should be booked in advance. SweetMe Hot Spring features separate public baths for men and women.

claim: Yangmingshan National Park is reached from Jiantan MRT by bus R5, S15, or S17, with S15 best as it passes Xiaoyoukeng, Lengshuikeng and Qingtiangang trailheads; Qixing Mountain (1,120m) is a 2-3 hour hike.
quote: From MRT Jiantan station... take either city bus R5 or small bus S15 or S17 to Yangmingshan station. Bus S15 from Jiantan is best... Qixing Mountain (1,120msl) is the highest mountain in Taipei... about 2–3 hours for the entire hike.

claim: Yangmingshan offers volcanic sulphur features at Xiaoyoukeng (fumaroles, steam vents) and free public hot springs at Lengshuikeng for soaking after a hike.
quote: Xiaoyoukeng... a large volcanic steam vent area with hiking trails, fumaroles, sulfur deposits, and natural hot springs... Lengshuikeng is a public hot spring facility... a perfect rest spot to soak your limbs in hot sulphuric waters after the long Yangmingshan hike.

claim: The Maokong Gondola is reached via the Wenhu MRT line to Taipei Zoo station; the line has 4 stations (Taipei Zoo, Taipei Zoo South, Zhinan Temple, Maokong) with the highest concentration of teahouses along Lane 38 near the top.
quote: get off at the last stop of the Metro's Wenhu Line—Taipei Zoo Station... The highest concentration of tea shops can be found about a 10 minute walk south of the Maokong gondola station along Lane 38 including Mountain Tea House, Found Your Tea and the Big Tea Pot.

claim: Maokong gondola single fares are NT$70/100/120 by distance, or a one-day unlimited pass is NT$300, with a crystal-floor cabin upgrade at +NT$50 per trip.
quote: A regular cabin one-day pass costs NT$300 for unlimited gondola rides, with an upgrade to crystal cabin adding NT$50 per person per trip. For individual journeys, regular fares are TWD 70 (1 stop), TWD 100 (2 stops) and TWD 120 (3 stops).

claim: Shifen and Pingxi are reached by TRA train from Taipei to Ruifang then the Pingxi branch line, which stops at both villages for the waterfall, old streets, and year-round sky-lantern releases.
quote: Take a northbound TRA train from Taipei Main Station to Ruifang Station, then transfer to the charming Pingxi Branch Line. This train stops directly at both Shifen and Pingxi stations.

claim: The annual Pingxi Sky Lantern Festival mass releases fall on Feb 27 (Pingxi) and Mar 3 (Shifen) in 2026, and the small Pingxi line gets overwhelmed with long waits during events.
quote: The Pingxi Sky Lantern Festival returns in 2026 with two spectacular dates: February 27th in Pingxi and March 3rd in Shifen... The Pingxi Line is a small local railway that becomes overwhelmed during festival events.

claim: June in Taipei is hot and very humid (highs ~32C, 81-88% humidity, heat index near 43C) and is one of the wettest months with ~326mm rain over ~15.5 days, from tail-end plum rains and heavy afternoon downpours.
quote: June temperatures in Taipei vary between a high-temperature of 32°C... humidity between 81% and 88%... In Taipei, in June, it is raining for 15.5 days, with typically 326mm (12.83") of accumulated precipitation.

claim: Din Tai Fung's original shop opened on Xinyi Road in 1972; the original site is now takeaway-only, with dine-in across the street in a 330-seat four-storey flagship opened 2020, the only branch in the Michelin Guide.
quote: the first shop opened on Xinyi Road... The former flagship eatery is now takeaway-only, but dine-in service is available on the other side of the street in a 330-seater four-storey venue inaugurated in 2020.

claim: Din Tai Fung's Xinyi Road location holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand and is famed for xiaolongbao made with exactly 18 folds.
quote: Din Tai Fung (Xinyi Road) – Taipei - a MICHELIN Guide Restaurant

claim: Taiwanese beef noodle soup features tender braised beef, chewy noodles and a savory soy-based broth spiced with star anise and Chinese herbs; top Taipei spots include Lin Dong Fang, Lao Wang Ji and Yong Kang Beef Noodles.
quote: tender braised beef, chewy noodles and a savory soy-based broth spiced with star anise and Chinese herbs

claim: Two tea houses — Chun Shui Tang in Taichung and Hanlin Tea Room in Tainan — both claim to have invented bubble tea in the mid-1980s; a 2019 court ruling found the drink could not be patented.
quote: Two tea houses — Chun Shui Tang in the central city of Taichung and Hanlin Tea Room in the southern city of Tainan — both claim to have invented the drink

claim: Chun Shui Tang dates its invention of bubble milk tea to 1987 when staff member Lin Hsiu Hui added tapioca to iced tea on a whim.
quote: World's Birthplace of Bubble Tea | Chun Shui Tang Humanistic Tea House

claim: Fuhang Soy Milk, established 1958 on the 2nd floor of Huashan Market near Shandao Temple MRT, is Taipei's most famous breakfast shop; its thick soy milk costs NT$30 and it won a Michelin Bib Gourmand in the 2018 Taipei guide.
quote: Fuhang was established in 1958, and this fame catapulted after it bagged a Michelin Bib Gourmand award in the inaugural (2018) Taipei Michelin guide.

claim: Classic Taiwanese breakfast items include shaobing (clay-oven rolls), youtiao (fried dough sticks), dan bing (egg pancakes), salty soy milk and rice balls.
quote: salty soy milk... rice balls... green onion pancakes

claim: Wistaria Tea House south of Da'an Park is Taipei's oldest kung-fu-style teahouse, set in a Japanese-era home that was a White Terror-era meeting spot for intellectuals and dissidents, serving fine oolong with Yixing teaware.
quote: Taipei's oldest "kung fu-style" teahouse... housed in a Japanese era home that was an underground meeting spot for artists, intellectuals, and dissidents during the later days of the White Terror period

claim: Maokong, on Taipei's edge and reachable by gondola, has 40+ traditional teahouses, some overlooking tea plantations or Taipei 101, producing local Baozhong and Tieguanyin oolongs.
quote: more than 40 teahouses in Maokong area, some of which overlook small tea plantation of even have views of Taipei 101

claim: Bingzan (冰讚) near Shuanglian MRT serves fresh mango shaved ice during mango season (roughly April–October); off-season, Yongkang Street shops use frozen mango.
quote: Bingzan (冰讚) in Taipei is the ultimate spot for mango shaved ice during mango season (April–October), located just a 5-minute walk from Shuanglian Station.

claim: Taipei bars rank highly on Asia's 50 Best Bars, including The Public House (#40) and To Infinity & Beyond (#41) in the top 50, plus Wu (Nothingness), Lab and Bar Mood in the extended 51-100 list.
quote: The Public House (Taipei) - Rank 40; To Infinity & Beyond (Taipei) - Rank 41

claim: Bar Mood, from bartender Nick Wu, is an elegant Taipei cocktail bar emphasising creative drinks and Taiwanese/Japanese whisky, with an illustrated menu featuring drinks like the rum-based 'Spice Raft'.
quote: Bar Mood is an elegant space from Taiwanese bartender Nick Wu, emphasising creative cocktails as well as Taiwanese and Japanese whisky.

claim: Draft Land serves all cocktails on tap, letting guests try before they buy, and is part of the Drinks Lab collective expanding across Asia.
quote: the cocktails are served on tap, which means you can try before you buy.

claim: Taipei's top specialty cafes include Simple Kaffa (by 2016 World Barista Champion Berg Wu, on the 88th floor of Taipei 101) and Fika Fika (Nordic-style, by WBC medalist James Chen).
quote: Simple Kaffa, founded by Berg Wu, the 2016 World Barista Champion... perched way up in Taipei 101, on the 88th floor.

claim: The EasyCard is a rechargeable contactless smart card costing NT$100 for the card itself, sold at any MRT station and convenience store, usable on MRT, buses, YouBike, and at 7-Eleven/FamilyMart/Hi-Life/OK Mart checkouts.
quote: The card itself costs only 100 TWD... You can buy it from any convenience store or MRT station in the country. Major chains like 7-Eleven, FamilyMart, Hi-Life, and OK Mart sell EasyCards.

claim: EasyCard MRT rides are about 20% cheaper than single-journey tokens and give a small transfer discount (NT$8) between MRT and bus within one hour.
quote: EasyCard MRT rides are about 20% cheaper than buying single-journey tokens... EasyCard does give a small discount when transferring (adults TWD 8) from a Taipei MRT to a bus (or vice versa) within one hour.

claim: The Taoyuan Airport MRT to Taipei Main Station costs NT$160; the Express takes ~39 min and Commuter ~53 min, running roughly 5:55 AM to 11:35 PM (not 24/7); bus 1819 is NT$135 and runs 24 hours in about an hour; taxis cost NT$1,200-1,500. Songshan Airport (TSA) is a smaller in-city airport with its own MRT stop handling mostly domestic and a few international flights.
quote: Express train: 39 minutes... Both cost 160 TWD... Last departure at 11:35 PM... Bus #1819... Cost: 135 TWD... Operates 24 hours... Taxi... 1,200-1,500 TWD... Songshan Airport, a smaller airport in the Taipei City center, which has mostly domestic flights and a few international ones.

claim: June in Taipei is the plum rain season: hot and humid with daytime highs near 33C, ~20 rainy days and one of the highest rainfall totals of the year, usually as brief heavy afternoon downpours, but before the main July-September typhoon season.
quote: June marks the plum rain season, so expect conditions to be quite hot and humid... heavy (although usually brief) late afternoon downpours... June is before the main typhoon season (July, August, and September).

claim: Taipei June daytime highs reach around 33C (91F) with nights near 26C, humidity around 80-85%, so pack light breathable fabrics plus rain gear, sun protection, and stay hydrated.
quote: Daytime highs reach around 33°C (91°F), with nights near 26°C (79°F)... Humidity levels hover around 79.5%... bring both rain gear and summer clothing. Light, breathable fabrics like cotton and linen are essential.

claim: Taipei MRT single-journey fares run NT$20-65, a one-day pass is about NT$180, and in 2026 fare gates accept contactless credit cards and mobile wallets (Apple Pay/Google Pay) though these earn no stored-value discounts.
quote: a fare range of NT$20-65 for single journeys, with one-day passes at approximately NT$180... contactless credit cards and mobile wallets (2026 updates).

claim: Eating, drinking, chewing gum or littering anywhere past the yellow line in MRT stations or on trains is banned and carries a fine of NT$1,500 to NT$7,500; priority seats should be given to elderly, disabled, pregnant, and those with young children.
quote: A fine of somewhere between NT$1,500 and NT$7,500 will be imposed for drinking, eating, chewing gum or betel nuts... Please give your seat to the disabled, elderly, pregnant women, passengers with young children.

claim: Taiwan uses the New Taiwan Dollar; cards are widely accepted in Taipei but night markets and small shops prefer cash, ATMs (including international-card ATMs at 7-Eleven and FamilyMart) are abundant, and tourist SIMs from Chunghwa/Taiwan Mobile/FarEasTone are sold at the airport for NT$300-500.
quote: tourist SIM at the airport from Chunghwa Telecom, Taiwan Mobile, or FarEasTone... NT$300-500... cards are widely accepted in Taipei and cities, smaller towns, night markets, and traditional shops often prefer cash. ATMs are abundant; 7-Eleven and FamilyMart... have international ATMs.

claim: US citizens can enter Taiwan visa-free for up to 90 days for tourism, with a passport valid at least 6 months beyond the stay; tipping is not customary in Taiwan.
quote: US citizens can visit Taiwan without a visa for up to 90 days for tourism... passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond your planned stay.

claim: For a short visit, central Ximending (near Ximen MRT) suits first-timers for food, shopping and nightlife; Zhongshan is best for dining; Xinyi for Taipei 101 luxury but farther from sights; anywhere a couple stops from Taipei Main Station is a good base.
quote: For a first trip to Taipei, staying in Ximending is recommended as this central area is near points of interest... Zhongshan is best for dining... Xinyi is best for luxury... anywhere a couple stops from Taipei Main Station is a great choice of location.

claim: A workable Taipei day groups attractions south-to-north: morning at Longshan Temple/Wanhua and CKS Memorial, midday Ximending lunch and Huashan 1914, late afternoon Elephant Mountain or Taipei 101, then a night market dinner.
quote: 8 AM: Longshan Temple ... 10 AM: CKS Memorial Hall ... Explore Ximending and lunch ... 4 PM: Elephant Mountain or Taipei 101 ... 7 PM: Linjiang Street (Tonghua) Night Market

claim: Jiufen sits about 1 to 1.5 hours from Taipei and needs roughly a half day (3-4 hours on site) to a full day to enjoy, with weekends running slower.
quote: It should take you between an hour and an hour and a half to get from Taipei to Jiufen ... a half-day (3-4 hours) is enough to see the main sights, but a full day allows for a more relaxed pace.

claim: Shilin Night Market runs roughly 5pm to midnight; vendors are set up by 5 but crowds peak at 7, so an early arrival gives 60-90 minutes of lower-stress eating.
quote: open from 5pm until midnight ... Most vendors are set up by 5 PM, but the crowds don't really build until 7, and arriving in the early window gives you 60-90 minutes of lower-stress eating before the rush.

claim: A three-day Taipei plan dedicates day 1 to the central urban core (CKS, Longshan, Yongkang St, Taipei 101, Elephant Mountain, night market), an entire day 2 to the Jiufen/Shifen/Yehliu northern coast trip, and day 3 to trendy inner neighborhoods like Zhongshan plus the National Palace Museum.
quote: Day 1: Central Taipei Urban Core ... Day 2: Northern Taiwan Coastal Excursion ... Yehliu Geopark, Jiufen Old Street, and Shifen ... Day 3: Trendy Inner-City Neighborhoods ... Zhongshan district

claim: Ximending is much livelier on weekends and at night, best saved for a Saturday or Sunday evening.
quote: Ximending is a lot more alive on weekends and at night, so if you're looking for that hustle-bustle atmosphere, consider visiting it on a Saturday or Sunday night.
